designDirection: Graphite studio with pale lime actions, visual effect families, consistent desktop navigation and persistent playback controls
designSystem:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE complete, high fidelity DESKTOP APPLICATION page, a crisp directly front-facing 16:10 landscape screenshot ideally 1600x1000 or larger, edge to edge app UI. No monitor, laptop, browser chrome, perspective presentation, collage, multiple screens, surrounding margin or watermarks. This is a redesigned AULA F75 mechanical keyboard control app, a precision creative instrument like a superb native design/audio tool. It must be truly usable, exceptionally composed, restrained and modern rather than a generic SaaS dashboard or gaming web landing page.
LOCKED DESIGN SYSTEM for every screen: graphite background #151719, sidebar #111315, main raised surfaces #1d2023, understated separators #303438, warm near-white text #f0f2eb, secondary text #a4aaa7, action accent pale lime #d8f879. Accent only on active controls, selected states and primary actions; cyan/teal/blue/amethyst light belongs inside keyboard previews, not page decoration. Excellent contrast. Elegant Geist/Satoshi-like sans, 30px semibold page title, 15px readable UI text, 12px minimum captions, tabular mono numbers. 8px spacing grid, comfortable 40px control heights, crisp thin precise icons, small 8-12px corner radii, subtle machined depth, no gratuitous gradients, no glass, no background glows, no neon borders, no huge marketing typography, no statistics unrelated to the task. Generous intentional negative space but useful app density.
LOCKED APP SHELL: left vertical sidebar roughly 200px wide, full height. At top a compact fine-line keycap emblem and wordmark 'AULA / F75'. Beneath a small device row 'AULA F75' and green status dot 'USB connected'. Main sidebar menu with simple line icons, in this exact order: 'Lighting', 'Key mapping', 'Macros', 'Profiles', 'Games'. Bottom of sidebar: 'Settings', 'Advanced'. Sidebar selection uses a quiet graphite rounded row, lime icon and slim lime indicator, not a big neon block. Main work area starts to the right with 32px padding. Upper-right consistent profile dropdown 'Daily driver' and small utility icon. Bottom persistent transport bar across work area: tiny keyboard/wave thumbnail, 'Aurora', secondary 'Automatic · Playing', subdued global pause and stop icons, and right-hand text 'Live on keyboard' with green dot. This transport bar is present even outside lighting, keeping playback status unambiguous. No account/avatar/cloud/dashboard sales UI.
Keyboard visual when requested: accurate ANSI 75% AULA F75 six-row layout, function row with separated Esc, arrow cluster lower-right and a small knob at top-right. Show the entire board in wide straight top-down orthographic view with tasteful subtle physical keycap depth, dark keycaps, legible legends, and colored LEDs softly illuminating individual keys. It should read as a controllable on-screen keyboard canvas, not an enormous product photograph or angled render. Use green-to-cyan-to-blue lighting for Aurora; dark neutral nonselected keys. Draw realistic wide Shift, Enter and Space keys. All labels fully visible, no ellipsized names.

pages.prompt:

Beneath toolbar a curated 3-column by 2-row library of SIX large visual effect previews, each using a tiny actual keyboard-shaped light pattern rather than abstract photos. Lighting selected; subnavigation Automatic / Typing / Audio / Per-key with Typing active. Page heading 'Lighting', subtitle 'Make every keystroke visible.'
Center top large keyboard preview with cyan expanding concentric rings originating at the G key, not a rainbow wash. PAGE 3 OF 10 — LIGHTING / AUDIO. Fresh standalone full application screenshot matching reference design exactly. Same sidebar Lighting selected. Main heading 'Lighting', subtitle 'Let your keyboard follow the music.' Same four subtabs, Audio active.
The central wide top-down keyboard preview displays frequency bars rising from bottom keys: calm lime-to-cyan-to-blue columns of varying heights, clearly attached to keys. Beneath it an integrated source strip with speaker icon, 'System audio', small source selector 'Speakers', green 'Receiving audio', and a small understated horizontal input level meter. This is the only page needing audio signal visualization, no unrelated graphs.
Below a toolbar 'Sound families' and search, and four roomy visual keyboard preview tiles in two columns: 'Spectrum' selected, 'Pulse', 'Beat ripples', 'Sparkle'. A fine explanatory line 'Variations and response settings live in the inspector.'
Right inspector heading 'Spectrum', description 'Frequency bands across your keyboard.' 'Variation' dropdown 'Bars', 'Response' slider 'Balanced', 'Sensitivity' slider 'Auto', 'Smoothing' slider '60%', 'Brightness' slider '70%', a palette strip of lime/cyan/blue and 'Edit palette'. Small low-key button 'Change audio source'. Primary lime 'Save preset'. Bottom persistent transport says 'Spectrum', 'Audio · Playing', small pause/stop and right 'Following system audio'. Do not imply microphone recording; this follows PC playback. Polished usable native app, no giant decorative waveform, no marketing imagery.
pages.refinement:
Use case: ui-mockup. Make ONE precise correction to this existing AULA F75 Audio page screenshot. Preserve the entire layout, sidebar, all text, inspector, tile library, typography, colors, spacing, buttons, footer and keyboard geometry exactly. Change ONLY the contents of the LARGE keyboard preview.
The keyboard visualizer must display equalizer columns by illuminating ENTIRE physical keycaps, not by drawing miniature bar charts on top of the keys. Remove every little equalizer/bar graphic from key surfaces including Space. Retain normal white key legends. To depict frequency columns, light contiguous bottom-up groups of whole keys in each x column at different heights. Example: left columns 1-2 bottom keys lit green, center columns 3-4 rows lit cyan, right columns 1-3 lower rows lit blue. Upper keys above a column's height remain dark charcoal. Each lit key is a single smooth colored RGB light cell with a soft edge backlight and no symbols other than its ordinary key legend. The real keyboard LEDs are the pixels. Keep the complete six-row keyboard with function row, arrows and knob. Keep the small actual audio input level meter BELOW the keyboard unchanged; it is valid UI. Do not change anything outside the large keyboard. One full-size landscape screenshot, no border or collage.

This screen is an editor, not another catalog. Main canvas is a very large complete straight overhead F75 keyboard, dark neutral gray keycaps, a tasteful blue backlight on most keys, and warm amber W A S D keys. Four selected keys W A S D have a distinct thin lime selection outline, with small label '4 keys selected' above the canvas. Leave authentic 75% key layout, arrows and knob. Above the canvas a compact left toolbar with arrow selection, brush, fill and eyedropper tools, separated undo and redo. Below canvas a slim row of selection shortcuts 'All keys', 'WASD', 'Arrows', 'Function row', 'Clear selection'. A second spacious lower row 'Saved palettes' showing a few deliberate palette strips named 'Ocean', 'Ember', 'Monochrome'; avoid a dense card grid.
Right inspector 'Selection', readable 'W, A, S, D'. Large tasteful square color picker with hue strip, selected warm amber swatch, hex field '#FFB85C', R G B inputs. 'Brightness' slider '75%'. One clear primary lime action 'Apply colors', secondary 'Save palette'. Small explanatory text 'Applies to the selected keys.' Bottom transport says 'Custom colors', 'Per-key · Active' and 'Live on keyboard'. Visually an excellent precise creative tool with no fake layer system, no analytics and no duplicate effect list.

PAGE 5 OF 10 — KEY MAPPING. Produce a fresh complete standalone page matching the attached master application's visual system and shell exactly. Sidebar 'Key mapping' selected; no Lighting subtabs on this page. Header 'Key mapping', subtitle 'Make the layout work for you.' Profile dropdown Daily driver stays top-right.
Below header a quiet layer segmented selector 'Default layer' selected / 'Fn layer'. Main wide workspace: a full accurate F75 keyboard in straight overhead view with almost-neutral dark gray keys and white readable labels, NO rainbow lighting on the mapping canvas. Select physical Caps Lock with a lime outline. A small readable floating annotation immediately under its position says 'Caps Lock → Escape'. Show function row keys subtly locked with a tiny lock legend and help 'Function keys use fixed firmware assignments.' Leave other keys fully legible. Above canvas label 'Choose a key to change its action'. Below keyboard a calm assignment table with heading 'Changed keys', columns 'Physical key', 'New action', 'Layer', rows 'Caps Lock' → 'Escape' / Default, and 'Right Alt' → 'Menu' / Default, each row has revert icon. Small '2 unsaved changes' status above table, not fake analytics.
Right inspector separated by a thin vertical rule: heading 'Caps Lock', secondary 'Default layer'. Section 'Assign an action' with category tabs 'Key' selected / 'Shortcut' / 'Media'. Dropdown 'Escape'. Below a readable keycap preview 'Esc' with arrow from a smaller keycap 'Caps'. A concise explanation 'This changes what the key sends. Its label stays the same.' Primary lime 'Save to keyboard', secondary 'Restore this key'. Small inline note with cable icon 'USB connection required to save'. Bottom persistent global transport retains Aurora / Automatic · Playing, pause and stop, Live on keyboard. Keep page practical, spacious and refined with readable typography and no code identifiers.

PAGE 6 OF 10 — MACROS. New complete standalone screenshot in the exact same app shell, colors, typography and proportions as master reference. Sidebar Macros selected. Header 'Macros', subtitle 'Record a sequence. Fine-tune every step.' Profile Daily driver top-right. Header action 'Record macro' with a tiny red record dot and otherwise neutral control styling.
IMPORTANT current product limitation must be honest and highly readable in a subtle inline informational strip: 'Saved on this computer. Keyboard playback is not available yet.' Do NOT show a working key trigger, upload macro button or fake enabled device playback.
Main layout is a useful sequence editor, not another grid of effect cards. Within content, a slim 225px macro list at left headed 'My macros' with search and three entries 'Paste without formatting' selected, 'Quick greeting', 'Open terminal'. Small '+' for creating another macro. Large center editor with title 'Paste without formatting' and quiet rename icon. A restrained horizontal timeline ruler 0 ms, 60 ms, 120 ms, 180 ms. Three tracks Ctrl, Shift, V with modest key-down/up duration blocks in desaturated lime. Beneath timeline show a readable ordered event table with rows 'Press Ctrl', 'Press Shift', 'Press V', 'Release V', 'Release Shift', 'Release Ctrl' and corresponding short delays, each with drag handle. This visualization describes key events, not sound. Toolbar 'Add key', 'Add delay', undo, redo. Most of page remains clean with generous space and clear order.
Right inspector roughly 250px: 'Sequence settings', 'Name' field 'Paste without formatting', 'Timing' Recorded / Fixed with Recorded selected, editable 'Default delay' 30 ms, 'Repeat' dropdown Once. Meaningful small summary '6 events · 180 ms'. Lime primary action 'Save macro', secondary 'Export'. Global bottom transport still Aurora / Automatic · Playing with pause/stop and Live on keyboard. No gratuitous graphs, no nested cards within cards, no huge panels filled with tiny illegible text.
pages.refinement:
Use case: ui-mockup. Correct ONLY the three horizontal key-hold blocks in the timeline of this existing AULA F75 Macros screenshot. Preserve all other pixels/layout/text/surfaces/menus/colors/sidebar/footer/inspector/event table.
The event table is the authority: Ctrl down at 0 ms and released at 180 ms; Shift down at 30 ms and released at 150 ms; V down at 60 ms and released at 120 ms. The timeline ruler stays 0,60,120,180 ms. Extend the CTRL track's horizontal bar to span the ENTIRE 0 to 180 ms timeline width. The SHIFT track bar must span 30 to 150 ms, inset one-sixth from both ends of the timeline. V track must span 60 to 120 ms, exactly the middle third of the timeline. Thus Ctrl is longest, Shift medium, V shortest, all center aligned. In the bars use only short labels 'Ctrl held', 'Shift held', 'V held'; remove the incorrect numeric range labels from inside the bars. Keep the ruler, keys at left, table values, 6 events · 180 ms summary, all buttons, existing info notice and main navigation exactly unchanged. No redesign. Return the entire same standalone landscape application screenshot with this targeted timeline fix.

pages.prompt:

This page must use an elegant spacious LIST layout, not repeat the lighting grid. Main area broad left, narrower right detail panel. Left top a search field 'Search profiles'. Below three beautifully composed large horizontal profile rows, about 150px high, separated by fine rules. Each row has a well-rendered small entire keyboard thumbnail at left, big readable name, a brief usage description and a few restrained setup details. Row one 'Daily driver' selected and marked small green 'Active'; green/cyan Aurora thumbnail, description 'A little color for everyday work.', details 'Aurora · 2 key changes'. Row two 'Focus', dim warm amber keyboard thumbnail, description 'Warm light. Fewer distractions.', details 'Night light · Default keys'. Row three 'Play', dark board with cyan WASD and arrows, description 'Your game-day layout.', details 'WASD focus · 4 key changes'. Row controls small overflow menus and Apply button for inactive profiles. Preserve ample open space below for a calm usable app, no stats.
Right detail panel heading 'Daily driver' with rename icon, miniature palette/keyboard thumbnail. Grouped flat summary sections 'Lighting' — 'Aurora / Northern lights', 'Brightness' — '70%', 'Key mapping' — '2 changes', 'Macros' — '3 saved locally'. Tiny helper 'Macro playback is not available yet.' Clear button 'Update from current setup' in lime, secondary actions 'Duplicate' and 'Export profile'. This is a future UI concept for saving a complete setup, not a cloud service: no accounts, online sync, analytics, avatars or team features.

PAGE 8 OF 10 — GAMES. Fresh complete single desktop application screenshot using the reference's same sidebar, header scale, surface colors, lime accent and bottom transport. Sidebar Games selected. Header 'Games', subtitle 'Your keyboard is the playing field.' Daily driver profile dropdown upper right. No lighting subtabs.
Main workspace broad center with large real F75 keyboard in a straight overhead orthographic view. Its dark keycaps themselves form the game pixels: a contiguous short lime snake made of 6 whole adjacent lit keys near middle rows, and one warm coral lit key as food elsewhere. Unlit keys remain dark; no tiny games or pixel icons printed inside individual keys, no replacement monitor game board. A small discreet 'Paused' tag above canvas. Below the board a readable 'Choose a game' toolbar and search, then six spacious visual mini-keyboard game tiles in 3 columns, labeled 'Snake' selected, 'Pong', 'Breakout', 'Memory', 'Reaction', 'Rhythm'. A small text line '14 games' without claiming 14 distinct categories. Each preview clearly shows a simple different arrangement of lit keys; no comic illustrations.
Right inspector heading 'Snake', description 'Eat the light. Keep your tail clear.' A neat small meaningful score row 'Score 6' and 'Best 18'. 'Difficulty' segmented Easy / Normal / Fast, Normal selected. 'Controls' with four arrow keycaps and 'Move', a Space keycap 'Pause'. Clear primary lime 'Resume game', secondary 'Restart'. Short helper 'Lighting resumes when you leave the game.' Bottom transport now says 'Snake', 'Game · Paused', with play and stop, and right 'Keyboard game active'. Beautiful restrained precision tool with a playful keyboard canvas; no leaderboards, online multiplayer, avatars, decorative charts or huge arcade title graphics.

PAGE 9 OF 10 — SETTINGS. Fresh full-screen standalone page retaining reference's EXACT sidebar, typography, colors and app shell. Sidebar Settings selected near bottom, not Lighting. Header 'Settings', subtitle 'Set it once. Make it yours.' Top-right profile Daily driver and quiet small status 'Changes saved'. Do not show a giant keyboard preview or effect gallery on this page.
Use an excellent native settings layout: two calm broad columns of flat grouped settings rows, understated separators, good vertical spacing, labels aligned left and values or switches aligned right. Left column headed 'Keyboard'. First section small neutral top-down F75 device thumbnail about 180px wide next to 'AULA F75' and green 'Connected via USB-C', understated 'Reconnect' link. Rows 'Debounce' with '4 ms' numeric stepper and tiny helpful description 'Time before a new keypress is accepted.' Row 'Onboard lighting' dropdown 'Rainbow' and smaller note 'Runs directly on the keyboard.' Row 'Onboard brightness' slider '70%'; row 'Wireless sleep' dimmed dropdown '10 minutes' and explanatory 'Available in wireless mode'. A compact secondary button 'Read keyboard settings'. Do not invent a firmware updater.
Right column headed 'Application'. Three switch rows: 'Launch at sign-in' on; 'Keep running in the tray' on with small description 'Closing the window keeps your lighting active.'; 'Resume last effect' on. Next group 'Appearance' dropdown 'Dark'. Next group 'Updates' label 'Version 0.2.1' with button 'Check for updates'. An understated 'About this app' link. At bottom of left column separate 'Reset keyboard' text action with a brief 'Restores the keyboard’s factory settings.' Do not make destructive controls visually dominant.
Persistent global bottom transport continues Aurora / Automatic · Playing, pause/stop and Live on keyboard. This should be a wonderfully clear, readable preferences page, no dashboard metrics, no irrelevant graphs, no four levels of nested cards.

PAGE 10 OF 10 — ADVANCED / DIAGNOSTICS AND LAYOUT CALIBRATION. New single full application page in exactly the reference's visual language and shell. Sidebar Advanced selected at bottom. Main header 'Advanced', subtitle 'Diagnostics and layout calibration.' Daily driver dropdown top-right. Header secondary action 'Export diagnostics'.
Avoid the clutter of a developer console. Upper main area has two balanced functional regions. Broad left region 'Layout calibration', very short instruction 'Press a key to check its position.' Show a medium full top-down F75 keyboard with neutral gray keys, only Esc highlighted lime, and a neat adjacent readout 'Detected key: Escape' / 'Mapped correctly' with green check. Tiny toolbar 'Test a key' selected and 'Calibrate layout'; secondary button 'Start calibration'. Do not show a terminal over the keyboard.
Right region 'Connection checks' uses readable flat checklist rows with precise thin check icons: 'Keyboard detected' / 'USB-C', 'Live lighting' / 'Available', 'Settings access' / 'Available', 'Global key capture' / 'Active'. Button 'Run checks again'. Small 'Last checked just now'.
Lower main area a single purposeful compact panel titled 'Activity log' with search field and quiet filter 'All events'. Show 5 concise left-aligned mono log rows with timestamps and clear status coloring, such as '10:42:18  Connected to AULA F75', '10:42:18  USB settings available', '10:42:19  Aurora started at 20 fps', '10:42:19  Global key capture active', '10:42:22  Escape mapped correctly'. Utility links 'Copy log' and 'Clear'. A subtle collapsible bottom row 'Backup and restore' with secondary 'Save snapshot' and 'Restore snapshot'. No raw hexadecimal protocol dumps unless expanded. No scary warnings or fake errors.
Persistent global transport Aurora / Automatic · Playing, pause/stop and Live on keyboard. Clear hierarchy, excellent alignment and contrast, precision without unnecessary complexity. This page should feel as finished as the main lighting screen.
